title: State v. Ravi Shankar (NDPS)
text: The accused, Ravi Shankar, was convicted by the Sessions Court under the NDPS Act for possession of commercial quantity of narcotic drugs. This appeal challenges the conviction on grounds of non-compliance with Section 50 of the NDPS Act, which requires search of a person to be conducted in the presence of a Gazetted Officer or a Magistrate if the accused so desires. The High Court examines the evidence of the police witnesses. The mandatory requirements of Section 50 were duly complied with as the accused was given the option and waived it in writing. The recovery is established beyond doubt. The conviction under the NDPS Act is upheld. However, considering the accused's cooperation during investigation, the sentence is reduced to the minimum prescribed under the NDPS Act with fine. The complainant is the State.
